m0010.summary: From London after Edward VII's funeral, Sabugosa tells Queen Amélie that the King intends to speak to the Queen so that Soveral, the Portuguese minister, can take up 'the matter' with her; news tomorrow.
m0010.en:
Today the King intends to speak to the Queen so that Soveral may take up the matter with her. I hope to give news
tomorrow. Sabugosa.

Notes. From the decode of the time on the card m0008, in telegraphic Portuguese without articles. The King is George V (Edward VII died on 6 May and was buried on 20 May 1910); the Queen is probably
Queen Alexandra, as in the telegram of 24 May. Soveral is the Marquis of Soveral, Portuguese minister in London
[our identification]. "The matter" is the decoder's word; the telegram of 24 May (m0012-13) says what it is.

m0012.summary: Queen Alexandra received Sabugosa with kind words; the King (George V) ended by saying he would see to getting him married; he has not seen the Princess; Soveral will handle the negotiation. The British marriage project for Manuel II in May 1910.
m0012.en:
Queen Alexandra received me last night and said very kind words to me [?]. His Majesty the King ended by saying
[?va] [?] [?count] [?at ease]: "I will see to getting him married." I had no opportunity to see the Princess. Soveral
says [he] will go to handle the [?further] negotiation. Sabugosa.

Notes. From the decode of the time on m0005 and m0004, with the decoder's question marks kept as holes. The
decoder wrote "tratar ei" (tratarei, "I will see to"), so the words "I will see to getting him married" are probably
the King's, at the end of what he said, not Sabugosa's comment. "Him" is presumably King Manuel II; the Princess is
not named in the text. "va" stands out of alphabetical place (0539 belongs before "me" 2013), so the decoder's "va"
is probably wrong.

m0016.summary: Sabugosa thanks the Queen, then at Naples, for a telegram that set his heart at rest, assures her of his constant loyalty, and is glad of good news.
m0016.en:
I thank Your Majesty with lively gratitude for the telegram, which has set my heart at rest. I am and always will be
the same. I am very glad of the good news and the demonstrations. I am writing. I kiss Your Majesty's hand. Sabugoza.

Notes. The coded words (from "veio" to "mesmo") come from the decode of the time on m0009; the rest is in clear on
the telegram. The code has the infinitive "ser" where the sense wants "sou" (I am). The year 1904 is from the
decode's date 24-4-04; the Naples stamp gives 24 April.

m0014.summary: Duplicate copy ('ampliation') of a 52-word code telegram signed Sabugoso, to Paris, the day after King Carlos's telegram of 12 May 1903 (targets/carlos1903).

snip.cap: Telegram from London received at Necessidades on 24 May 1910: code groups struck through by the decoder, 1738 circled
snip.credit: Arquivo Nacional Torre do Tombo, PT/TT/CAM/M14, image m0012, via DigitArq

system: One-part (alphabetical) Portuguese telegraph code: five-digit groups 11501-23400 carry words from a to h, four-digit groups 0139-9019 words from i to v; names spelled in pieces (Soveral = So / ver / al).
